title: Responsive Web Design Practice
description: Practise the twelve ideas in this Responsive Web Design course. Choose an answer, then read why it fits the example.

exercises.question: Why keep zoom enabled?
options: Some readers need larger text and controls
Zoom prevents all links from working
exercises.explanation: A viewport is the area a browser uses to show a page. A viewport meta tag helps mobile browsers use the device width for the layout.

exercises.question: What stops the content getting too wide?
options: The number of paragraphs
The 60rem maximum in min()
exercises.explanation: A box can use most of the available width while also having a maximum width. This avoids both cramped phones and very long lines.

exercises.question: Why use height:auto with a flexible image width?
options: To keep the picture's shape
To make every image a square
exercises.explanation: A responsive image can shrink to fit its parent while keeping its shape. Auto height keeps the original width-to-height ratio.

exercises.question: What allows a flex row to make another row?
options: text-align: center
flex-wrap: wrap
exercises.explanation: Flexbox can wrap items onto a new row when there is not enough space. A gap adds space without needing manual margins on every item.

exercises.question: What does auto-fit decide?
options: How many columns can fit the available space
How many letters each card can contain
exercises.explanation: An auto-fit grid chooses how many columns can fit. minmax gives each column a useful minimum and lets it share extra room.

exercises.question: Which layout is the starting layout here?
options: A permanent fixed-width desktop layout
One stacked column
exercises.explanation: A media query applies styles only when a viewport rule matches. Start with a simple small-screen layout, then add roomier choices.

exercises.question: What does clamp provide?
options: A minimum, a preferred value and a maximum
A fixed number of words
exercises.explanation: clamp chooses a value between a minimum and maximum. It can let a heading grow gently as the viewport grows.

exercises.question: Why leave space between touch controls?
options: To stop keyboard users reaching them
To reduce accidental taps on the wrong control
exercises.explanation: Touch users need controls that are easy to select. Padding and spacing help keep neighbouring choices apart.

exercises.question: What does overflow-wrap help prevent?
options: Long text pushing out of its box
Every paragraph having more than one sentence
exercises.explanation: Long links or words can force a box wider than its screen. overflow-wrap lets a long piece of text break when needed.

exercises.question: Which part should scroll horizontally here?
options: The entire page and every paragraph
The table region
exercises.explanation: A table may need more width than a phone. A named scroll area can keep the table readable without making the whole page scroll sideways.

exercises.question: What width does this @container rule check?
options: The chosen ancestor container width
Always the whole monitor width
exercises.explanation: A container query checks the size of a chosen parent box. A card can adapt to a narrow sidebar even on a wide screen.

exercises.question: Why test a long title?
options: Long titles make CSS stop loading
Real content can take more space than a short sample
exercises.explanation: A responsive layout needs testing with real words and larger text. A design can fit empty boxes yet fail when a title gets long.
